release.note: Source ZIP for Windows, macOS, or Linux. It needs Python 3.11 or newer. It is not a standalone app.

presets.name: Developer
presets.goal: Lock the screen when you step away from code, and optionally start the guard by voice.

presets.name: Office work
presets.goal: Protect an open-plan desk: lock when you leave, react when someone stands behind you.

presets.name: Study
presets.goal: Lock a laptop in a library or shared room if you walk off, with a simulator to learn the rules first.

presets.name: Creator
presets.goal: Point with one hand, click with a pinch, and visually clap to stop hand control.

presets.name: Desk privacy
presets.goal: The smallest setup: one camera, one rule, lock when the desk is empty or crowded.

features.name: Local dashboard and typed commands
features.summary: Runs at 127.0.0.1 on this computer. Type active, inactive, or stop.

features.name: Safe simulator
features.summary: Practice every rule with fake observations. No camera, microphone, or desktop action.

features.name: Presence guard
features.summary: Counts people in a local camera view. Frames stay in memory. No identity recognition.

features.name: Privacy lock
features.summary: Requests a Windows lock after more than 30 seconds away, two people for 2 seconds, or a camera fault.

features.name: Boss Alert (playful demo)
features.summary: Opens a clearly labeled synthetic spreadsheet when a second person stays in view. Not a security feature.

features.name: Hand control (watch me, clap to stop)
features.summary: Optional local MediaPipe hand tracking: index pointer, middle/thumb left click, ring/thumb right click, visual two-hand clap to stop. Real pointer movement needs a separate permission.

features.name: Offline voice activation
features.summary: Vosk listens on this computer for the word active. Nothing is uploaded.

ai_tools.name: None
ai_tools.guidance: Nothing to set up. Jarvis does not use a language model.

ai_tools.name: Local Ollama
ai_tools.guidance: Free software that runs models on your own hardware. Jarvis has no Ollama connector; keep using it on its own.

ai_tools.name: OpenAI API
ai_tools.guidance: Jarvis has no OpenAI connector and never asks for an API key.

ai_tools.name: Anthropic API
ai_tools.guidance: Jarvis has no Anthropic connector and never asks for an API key.

ai_tools.name: ChatGPT subscription
ai_tools.guidance: Keep using ChatGPT in its own app. Jarvis does not connect to it.

ai_tools.name: Claude subscription
ai_tools.guidance: Keep using Claude in its own app. Jarvis does not connect to it.

ai_tools.name: Other
ai_tools.guidance: Jarvis does not connect to outside AI tools. Keep using yours on its own.

voice_options.name: Offline voice (Vosk)
voice_options.guidance: The guided voice setup supports Windows in this release. It listens locally for active and needs a microphone, optional packages, and a model you download. Use typed commands on other systems.

voice_options.name: My computer's built-in voice tools
voice_options.guidance: Guidance only. Windows Voice Access, macOS Voice Control, and Linux tools work on their own. Jarvis does not integrate with them.

voice_options.name: Existing ElevenLabs account
voice_options.guidance: Guidance only. Jarvis has no ElevenLabs connector and does not speak. Nothing is sent to ElevenLabs.

voice_options.name: No microphone
voice_options.guidance: Use typed commands. Everything works without a microphone.

tasks.title: Install Python 3.11 or newer
tasks.detail: Use the official installer. On Windows, tick Add python.exe to PATH.

tasks.title: Download the Jarvis source ZIP and unzip it
tasks.detail: Unzip to a folder you own, such as Documents. Then double-click Start-Jarvis.cmd on Windows, or run python -m jarvis.launcher.

tasks.title: Try the simulator first
tasks.detail: Start the safe demo and walk through away, back, and a second person. Nothing real happens.

tasks.title: Install the camera package
tasks.detail: Windows: double-click Install-Optional-Tools.cmd, choose 1: Camera, and confirm. On macOS or Linux, run python -m jarvis.install_tools and choose the same item. Packages go into this project's .venv; no device starts.

tasks.title: Install the offline voice packages
tasks.detail: Windows: double-click Install-Optional-Tools.cmd, choose 3: Offline voice, and confirm. On macOS or Linux, run python -m jarvis.install_tools and choose the same item. Packages go into this project's .venv; no device starts. Voice includes one checksum-verified source build.

tasks.title: Download a Vosk model into models/voice-en
tasks.detail: After installing Offline voice, choose a small English Vosk model, read its license, and unzip it so models/voice-en/conf/model.conf and models/voice-en/am/ exist. The optional-tools installer does not download voice archives.

tasks.title: Keep Windows automatic lock on
tasks.detail: Jarvis is an extra guard, not a replacement. Check Settings, Accounts, Sign-in options.

tasks.title: Confirm a spreadsheet app opens .xlsx files
tasks.detail: Boss Alert opens a synthetic workbook with your default spreadsheet app.

tasks.title: Practice hand control in the simulator
tasks.detail: Use the practice pad on the dashboard. Clap stops hand control only. Real cursor movement stays off unless you turn it on.

tasks.title: Install the local hand tracking packages
tasks.detail: Windows: double-click Install-Optional-Tools.cmd, choose 2: Camera + hand gestures, and confirm. On macOS or Linux, run python -m jarvis.install_tools and choose the same item. Packages go into this project's .venv; no device starts.

tasks.title: Install and verify the hand model
tasks.detail: Windows: Install-Optional-Tools.cmd option 2 or 4 downloads this official model into models/ and verifies its SHA-256. The portable optional-tools menu does the same. Use the link only for a manual download.

tasks.title: Save your preferences
tasks.detail: Local mode only, and only when you choose Apply. Writes runtime/setup-config.json. Nothing is armed.

tasks.title: Launch Jarvis with your plan
tasks.detail: Run this command from the unzipped Jarvis folder after completing the optional-tools menu. Hardware plans use the local .venv interpreter; simulator-only plans use Python. Actions stay disarmed until you arm them in the dashboard.
